transport: Two hops, and neither is direct. Battery ↔ LFP Connect gateway over a proprietary 'AEBus' RJ-45 link (rate and framing never stated). Gateway ↔ Victron over a straight CAT5 from the LFP Connect Card for Victron (a Slot 0 card, left-hand slot only) into VE.Can port A on a CCGX/Venus GX, terminated in port B, with the GX set to CANbus profile 'VE.Can & CAN-bus BMS (250 kbit/s)'.
refutedOnReview: REFUTED. Both cited PDFs exist and are correctly attributed, but I read both in full and neither contains a register map, so there is nothing for the two models to "share."  1. LFP CONNECT CARD VICTRON ENERGY USER MANUAL (PN LFP-CCRD-VCTRN) — fetched and text-extracted, 10 pages, complete. It contains ZERO register addresses, zero Modbus registers, zero CAN IDs/PGNs, no slave/node ID, and no baud rate for the Rolls s
gotchas: 250 kbit/s, not 500. The legacy generation runs the GX on 'VE.Can & CAN-bus BMS (250 kbit/s)'; the current S48-100LFP ESS and STACK-LV run BMS-CAN at 500 kbit/s. Same vendor, same battery chemistry, half the bit rate. This alone makes it a separate dialect and it is a documented fact, not an inference.

There is no direct wire from the battery. Closed loop requires the LFP Connect gateway plus a brand-specific LFP Connect Card, and the battery-side link is a proprietary bus called AEBus. Cabin Hub cannot listen to this battery without the vendor's own hardware in the path.

The manual warns not to plug the AEBus RJ-45 terminator into the gateway's 10/100 ethernet port, and not to run the ethernet port to a router WAN/modem port. Both are RJ45 and both will damage equipment. Same shape, different bus — the recurring hazard across this whole catalogue.
'VE.Can MPPTs cannot be used and are not yet supported' in this configuration.
Still sold: The Cabin Depot lists a 'Rolls 48V 6.65kWh LiFePO4 Battery S48-6650LFP'. So this is not purely historical — a Quebec cabin could have one bought recently. checked: 2026-07-31
unmappedReports: charge-voltage-limit / charge-current-limit / discharge-current-limit — the gateway's whole purpose is publishing these to Victron DVCC and the contract cannot express any of them, BMS low-voltage threshold, which the doc warns is displayed but is not the actual discharge limit
